item.title: Engineered mRNA-packaging virus-like particles enable efficient and precise mitochondrial base editing in vitro and in vivo.
item.abstract: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) base editors (mtBEs) are promising tools for studying and correcting pathogenic mtDNA mutations. However, the application of mtBEs is often hindered by substantial mtDNA-wide off-target editing that accumulates with prolonged mtBE expression resulting from plasmid DNA or viral delivery. To overcome this limitation, we developed mtBE-VLPs, a virus-like-particle (VLP) platform for transiently delivering mtBEs in vitro and in vivo with minimal off-target effects. While canonical protein-packaging VLPs yielded undetectable mtDNA base editing, engineered mRNA-packaging VLPs enabled efficient but transient mtBE cargo delivery. By iteratively engineering mRNA-packaging VLP compositions, we improved mtBE-VLP-mediated base editing efficiencies from less than 1% to greater than 50% across multiple target mtDNA loci in bulk populations of treated cultured cells. To further improve the packaging and delivery of certain mtBEs, we developed a strategy to selectively reduce mtBE cargo expression in VLP producer cells but not transduced cells, which increased VLP-mediated base editing efficiencies for certain mtBEs by 7.1-fold. Compared to plasmid DNA delivery in vitro , mtBE-VLPs exhibited equivalent on-target editing but 23- to 41-fold lower mtDNA-wide off-target editing, highlighting the improved editing specificity offered by transient mtBE delivery. mtBE-VLPs efficiently installed a pathogenic mtDNA mutation in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (88% efficiency) and corrected a pathogenic mtDNA mutation in a human patient-derived cell line (41% efficiency). Additionally, a single subretinal injection of mtBE-VLPs yielded 6-20% (average 12%) mtDNA base editing in the mouse retinal pigment epithelium with minimal mtDNA-wide off-target editing. These findings establish mRNA-packaging mtBE-VLPs as promising vehicles for efficient and precise mitochondrial base editing via transient mtBE delivery.

item.title: Self-extending DNA recording with stochastic and programmed writing
item.abstract: Recording cellular histories requires continued information accumulation while retaining earlier records. Infinite Printer couples DNA self-extension to regeneration of a writable terminal context. A single self-targeting prime-editing guide directs repeat extension, while base editing diversifies the accessible sequence in situ. A separate configuration uses auxiliary guides for specified payload writing. After three rounds of payload input, 4,436 distinct complete records contained identities from all three pools. Extended AC/AT records retained shared upstream marks, and complete-sequence readout distinguished endpoints sharing initial prefixes. Joint single-cell readout recovered 1,549 records and 7,669 combinations across 12,302 transcriptome-linked cell labels; spatial readout linked records to 11,330 capture spots. These results establish a resource for self-extending stochastic and programmed DNA recording with joint cellular and tissue readout, providing a foundation for future lineage applications.

item.title: Prime editing enables high-throughput identification and characterization of selective MutSβ inhibitors.
item.abstract: DNA mismatch repair (MMR) maintains genome stability but paradoxically drives expansion of pathogenic repeats responsible for trinucleotide repeat disorders. Attenuating repeat instability through targeted inhibition of MMR is therefore a therapeutic strategy of interest; however, progress is constrained by a lack of robust methods for defining and isolating MMR subpathways. We exploited features of prime editing to profile the effects of core MMR genes on thousands of programmed DNA mispairs in cells and resolved distinct MMR processes, including a noncanonical "loop-directed" mechanism. Guided by these results, we built a set of scalable reporters that detect loss of separable MMR processes and screened ∼72,000 small molecules for activity against MutSβ-directed MMR. This effort identified a novel series of MutSβ inhibitors that reduced (CAG) n expansion in a cell model. Altogether, this study establishes several methods for systematically interrogating MMR, with demonstrated capacity to identify inhibitors of therapeutic value.

item.title: Programmable Engineered Living Vehicles as Autonomous Biofactories for Synergistic Osteomyelitis Management and Bone Regeneration.
item.abstract: Conventional static biomaterials and synthetic nanomedicines struggle to penetrate recalcitrant biofilms and orchestrate tissue regeneration in deep-seated infections due to limited autonomous navigation and a lack of spatiotemporal responsiveness. Here, we conceptualize and develop a programmable engineered living vehicle (ELV) that functions as an autonomous biofactory for the synergistic management of drug-resistant osteomyelitis. Built upon a self-propelled Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 chassis with innate ecological dominance, these living biofactories are hierarchically equipped with environmental biosensors and logic-gated computing modules. Crucially, leveraging AlphaFold 3-guided molecular docking, we engineered multiscale thermo-responsive genetic logic circuits that enable precise, temperature-dependent biomanufacturing of bacteriolytic lysostaphin (LYS) and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) (≥37°C), coupled with a fail-safe thermal self-destruct mechanism (≥42°C). Furthermore, surface-engineered (DSS)6 peptides confer robust hydroxyapatite affinity, acting as a bone-homing navigation module. In a rat osteomyelitis model induced by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), intravenously deployed ELV biofactories autonomously navigate to the infected niche, actively penetrate biofilms, and outperform vancomycin in pathogen clearance. Concurrently, localized payload secretion reprograms the osteo-immune microenvironment, significantly accelerating bone repair. This work establishes a versatile paradigm for next-generation smart living therapeutics, bridging synthetic biology with micro-engineering to address complex clinical challenges.

item.title: From cell factories to photobiocatalysts: reengineering cyanobacteria for solar-driven chemical manufacturing.
item.abstract: To achieve more sustainable, light-powered chemical manufacturing, cyanobacterial engineering is expanding from conventional carbon-accumulating "cell factories" toward the complementary use of cyanobacteria as "whole-cell photobiocatalysts." This review critically examines this conceptual extension. By shifting the engineering focus from carbon-centric biosynthesis to electron- and energy-coupled catalysis, this emerging approach partially decouples target-product formation from the de novo assembly of CO2-derived carbon skeletons. Instead, it exploits photosynthetically generated reducing equivalents and ATP to support redox and energy-dependent enzymatic transformations, thereby reducing dependence on external cofactor- or energy-regeneration systems. We outline a multidimensional engineering framework that integrates carbon-flux redirection ("push"), coupling to photosynthetically generated reducing equivalents and ATP ("drive"), and product-removal-driven "pull" through secretion, volatilization, or in situ extraction. We further highlight advances in light-tolerant and stress-robust cyanobacterial chassis, together with emerging process strategies based on attached-growth and biofilm photobioreactors. We also critically consider genetic instability, variable enzyme-coupling efficiency, and scale-dependent light and mass-transfer limitations. Finally, we discuss the biophysical and energetic limits of light-to-chemical conversion, competition for reducing power, the largely conceptual potential of temporally decoupled light harvesting and dark-phase catalysis, and the need to select economically viable target products using rigorous techno-economic and life-cycle analyses. Collectively, this review provides conceptual and practical guidance for developing sustainable photosynthetic biomanufacturing platforms.

item.title: Adaptive Laboratory Evolution Rewires Pseudomonas putida for Resource-Efficient Acetate Assimilation.
item.abstract: Acetate is an attractive renewable two-carbon substrate for microbial biotechnology, but toxicity limits growth and carbon-use efficiency at process-relevant concentrations. Here, we used adaptive laboratory evolution to improve acetate tolerance in a genome-reduced strain of Pseudomonas putida and combined whole-genome sequencing, quantitative physiology, reverse engineering, transcriptomics, proteomics and 13C-acetate fluxomics to resolve the underlying adaptation mechanisms. Evolution under increasing acetate concentrations selected recurrent mutations in gacA and fabB, which encode a global response regulator and a fatty acid biosynthesis enzyme, respectively. Reverse engineering of these mutations recapitulated most of the evolved phenotype, including shorter lag phase and substantially higher biomass yield from acetate. Multi-omic analyses showed repression of type VI secretion systems, carbohydrate storage functions, fatty acid metabolism and oxidative stress-associated proteins, indicating resource reallocation away from costly stress and non-essential programs. Fluxomics further revealed reduced carbon cycling and increased glyoxylate shunt flux, consistent with improved acetate-carbon retention in biomass. These results establish acetate tolerance in P. putida as a resource-efficiency phenotype and identify gacA and fabB as actionable targets for acetate-based bioproduction.

item.title: Progress and perspectives in nitrogenase engineering in plants and yeast.
item.abstract: Crop productivity relies on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers, which entail significant economic and environmental costs. Engineering crop plants to produce nitrogenase allowing them to acquire nitrogen from the atmosphere offers a transformative approach to sustainable agriculture. However, engineering the nitrogenase pathway into eukaryotic cells poses significant challenges due to the enzyme metal clusters, high energy demands, and extreme sensitivity to oxygen. This review summarizes recent advances in nitrogenase engineering in yeast and plants. Progress has been made using a stepwise modular approach and a functional validation pipeline for core and ancillary nitrogenase proteins. Key milestones include recovery of NifH with in vitro activity from mitochondria and chloroplasts, production of NifB that is active upon isolation or after in vitro cluster reconstitution, production of NifB-co in yeast mitochondria, in vitro FeMo-co biosynthesis using proteins purified from yeast mitochondria, and recovery of nitrogenase components from transgenic rice with activity demonstrated in vitro. Complete nitrogenase activity in engineered yeast or plants has not yet been demonstrated. We discuss the importance of organelle targeting, the exploitation of natural diversity and engineered proteins, and synthetic biology tools for the assembly of multigene pathways. Finally, we present the main remaining obstacles, such as the assembly of functional NifDK in plants, integration with host metabolism and coordinated regulation, and we outline the prospects for the development of nitrogen-fixing crops.

item.title: Bacterial-fungal cross-kingdom interactions in synthetic consortia: boosting secondary metabolites and sustainable food fermentation.
item.abstract: Bacterial-fungal consortia (BFC) consistently outperform aseptic or single-species cultures in producing high-value secondary metabolites, yet the underlying cross-kingdom interaction mechanisms remain poorly understood. In food fermentations, BFCs enhance process robustness, substrate turnover, and bioactive profiles for sustainable functional foods. In these consortia, bacteria and fungi engage in complex cooperative and competitive interactions, involving signaling molecules, genetic regulation, and metabolic flux redistribution to enhance secondary metabolite yields. Based on the ecological compatibility and molecular communication mechanisms, a synthetic microbiology framework for constructing high-yield BFCs was proposed. This systematic approach included selecting appropriate coculture partners, setting up the BFC, and optimizing cultivation conditions. Functional BFCs can be effectively applied to: food fermentation, improving fermentation efficiency, nutritional value, flavor complexity, and food safety. The review provides an overview of BFCs for secondary metabolite production, with emphasis on their cross-kingdom communication mechanisms. It explores the construction and optimization of BFCs and their applications in food fermentation, identifying future directions for enhancing secondary metabolite yields.

item.title: Hyperproduction of a Fungal Natural Product, Calcarisarbulide A, From a Synthetic Transcriptional Cascade.
item.abstract: Effective hyperproduction of fungal natural products (NPs) is one of the challenges in their pharmaceutical development. Calcarisarbulide A (1) is a promising anti-liver-fibrosis NP from the endophyte Calcarisporium arbuscula. Here, based on a hybrid transcription factor used to awaken the cal gene cluster (GC) in C. arbuscula and genetic engineering to block the biotransformation of 1, a yield of 1.13 g/L was obtained. To produce 1 more safely and at higher yields, heterologous expression in Aspergillus was demonstrated. However, the yields of 1 were much lower in A. nidulans and A. terreus, likely due to the endogenous metabolism of 1. In A. oryzae, where 1 is not metabolized, a synthetic transcriptional cascade was developed from the A. nidulans afo GC to produce 1.31 g/L of 1. Further aspartic acid feeding led to a 2.62 g/L yield. Our work provides a new synthetic biology strategy for the efficient production of bioactive fungal NPs.

item.title: Mechanistic insights into atmospheric and room-temperature plasma (ARTP)-induced genomic alterations and phenotypic evolution in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
item.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Atmospheric and room-temperature plasma (ARTP) is a potent tool for microbial strain engineering; however, the mechanistic basis of its genome-wide mutagenic effects remains poorly understood. Utilizing Saccharomyces cerevisiae as a model, we performed a comprehensive characterization of the mutational landscape and DNA repair pathways elicited by ARTP. Under high-lethality conditions (~99% mortality), ARTP treatment induced a substantial mutational burden, with SNVs and InDels rates increasing 25.2- and 36.7-fold relative to untreated controls, respectively. These mutations exhibited a pronounced bias toward C-T/G-A and A-T/T-A substitutions and InDels within AT-rich regions. Remarkably, the frequency of loss of heterozygosity (LOH) surged 57.4-fold, suggesting a potent capacity for inducing DNA breaks. Through sectored colony assays, we demonstrate that ARTP primarily inflicts pre-replicative double-strand breaks (DSBs), with reciprocal crossovers serving as the predominant driver of terminal LOH. The distribution and pattern of LOH were also altered in ARTP-treated cells. Mechanistically, our study establishes that the translesion synthesis polymerases Rev1 and Pol ζ are indispensable for converting ARTP-induced lesions-likely pyrimidine dimers-into fixed point mutations. In contrast, Rad30 facilitates high-fidelity bypass across these dimers. The base excision repair pathway appears largely dispensable for the processing of these lesions. In contrast, the nucleotide excision repair pathway plays a predominant role in mitigating ARTP-induced mutations. Finally, the strategic application of iterative ARTP mutagenesis facilitated the rapid evolution of acetate-tolerant strains. Our findings provide fundamental insights into the molecular signatures of ARTP mutagenesis, offering a framework for its optimized application in directed evolution.
IMPORTANCE: While ARTP is a cornerstone of non-thermal mutagenesis in industrial biotechnology, its genetic impact has long been treated as a "black box." This study provides a high-resolution molecular dissection of ARTP-induced genomic alterations using a diploid yeast model. We demonstrate that ARTP is not merely a source of point mutations but a potent catalyst for pre-replicative double-strand breaks and extensive mitotic recombination. By elucidating the pivotal roles of specific DNA repair pathways in mutation fixation, we transition ARTP from a purely empirical screening tool to a mechanistically grounded platform for directed evolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical utility of this platform by evolving acetate-tolerant strains and identifying the underlying genetic drivers of their resilience.

item.title: Proteoliposome Preparation and Functional Reconstitution of Human Mitochondrial Transporters Via Wheat Germ Cell-Free Expression System.
item.abstract: Mitochondrial membrane proteins play a crucial role in the transport of metabolites essential to cellular metabolism, and their dysfunction is linked to a wide range of metabolic diseases. Here, we present a method for the expression, reconstitution, and analysis of members of the solute carrier family 25 (SLC25), the largest family of human mitochondrial transport proteins, using the wheat germ cell-free protein synthesis (WG-CFPS) system. This approach enables the generation of proteoliposomes containing a defined and highly purified protein species. This workflow enables efficient production of active membrane proteins without the limitations of a cell-based expression system, such as aggregation into inclusion bodies, the need for purification, and the cytotoxic effects of membrane protein overexpression. SLC25A11 and SLC25A21 proteins, as examples of human mitochondrial transporters, are directly translated into asolectin liposomes in the presence of the non-ionic detergent Brij-35. Later, to form proteoliposomes suitable for downstream transport assays, the proteins were reconstituted into a substrate-loaded liposome. The article provides detailed procedures for template preparation, cell-free expression, proteoliposome assembly, and validation of incorporated protein transport activity. This method, by reducing the time required to express, purify, and reconstitute membrane proteins, provides a platform for studying human mitochondrial metabolite transport activity. Once the reagents and plasmid are prepared, the complete work, from protein expression to functional analysis, can be completed within 3 days. © 2026 The Author(s). item.title: Sustainable biomanufacturing of rare ginsenosides from Panax notoginseng: a critical review.
item.abstract: Rare ginsenosides (e.g. C-K, Rg3, Rh2) hold therapeutic promise but are severely constrained by low natural abundance. This review critically examines the entire biomanufacturing pipeline from green extraction to multi-modal conversion and de novo biosynthesis. Unlike previous reviews focusing on single technologies, this work systematically evaluates physical, chemical, and biological strategies and proposes an integrated upstream-midstream-downstream framework. Physical and chemical conversion methods can produce rare ginsenosides from abundant common precursors in Panax notoginseng, yet suffer from harsh conditions, poor selectivity, and C-20 epimeric mixtures. Biotransformation offers high regioselectivity, mild conditions, and retention of the desired 20(S)-configuration. However, distinct challenges exist such as microbial whole-cell fermentation suffers from complex metabolic networks, long cycles, and difficult separation, while enzymatic catalysis faces high enzyme costs, poor stability, and single-step limitations. Notably, while de novo biosynthesis draws upon key enzyme genes from Panax notoginseng to theoretically eliminate plant dependence, facing metabolic burden, low titers, and high costs, remain far from industrial viability. We highlight biocatalytic strengths including enzyme-mediated precise deglycosylation and recent breakthroughs in directed enzyme engineering for single products. From a techno-economic perspective, enzymatic conversion remains the most competitive route for producing rare ginsenosides at present, whereas de novo biosynthesis currently lacks the efficiency and economic feasibility to replace it.

item.title: Metabolic engineering of Yarrowia lipolytica for higher fatty alcohol production
item.abstract: Fatty alcohols are versatile chemicals with growing demand across a broad range of industries, yet conventional production methods pose environmental challenges. Microbial biosynthesis offers a promising alternative, if hosts can be engineered to achieve high product titers. The industrially relevant oleaginous yeast Yarrowia lipolytica is well suited to this challenge because of its natural capacity for lipid metabolism. Here, we engineered Y. lipolytica W29 for fatty alcohol production by disrupting pathways involved in lipogenesis and fatty alcohol oxidation, identifying fatty alcohol oxidation as a major constraint on product accumulation. Initial engineering yielded fatty alcohol titers of 2.5 g/L from 40 g/L glucose. Subsequent optimization of media supplements and nutrient concentrations, combined with deletion of the citrate transporter CEX1 and addition of 1% Tergitol to the extractive culture medium, increased titers to 10.9 g/L in shake flasks with 80 g/L glucose and a carbon-to-nitrogen ratio of 60. Scaling the process to fed-batch bioreactor cultivation further increased titers to 19.4 g/L. These results demonstrate that combining metabolic engineering with medium and process optimization enables high-titer fatty alcohol production in Y. lipolytica.

item.title: The historical evolution of CHO cell line development for biologics production: 60 years and still counting.
item.abstract: Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells have played a central role in the production of therapeutic proteins since their initial isolation in the 1950s. Over the decades, scientific innovations have transformed CHO cells into the powerhouse of the biopharmaceutical industry. From rudimentary culture conditions and random integration of transgenes into the host genome, to synthetic biology, genetic engineering, high-performing chemically defined media, targeted transgene integration and AI-driven cell line development strategies, each decade has introduced transformative tools, knowledge, and insights to improve CHO cell line development and characterization processes. This review outlines the chronological history of the CHO cell line development process, decade by decade, highlighting central milestones and innovations, technological breakthroughs, and the role of key innovative steps that have enabled modern cell line development workflows and ultimately the industrial-scale manufacturing of biologics.

item.title: Microscale zero-valent iron enhances light-dependent inorganic carbon assimilation in a Shewanella oneidensis-Rhodopseudomonas palustris coculture.
item.abstract: Microbial carbon dioxide (CO2) fixation driven by solid electron donors is often constrained by interfacial electron transfer. Here, we evaluated microscale zero-valent iron (mZVI) in an illuminated, anoxic coculture of Shewanella oneidensis and Rhodopseudomonas palustris using physiological, isotopic, electrochemical and metatranscriptomic analyses. Under photoautotrophic conditions, 200 mg L-1 mZVI increased the peak optical density at 600  nm (OD600) from 0.36 to 0.80 and mixed-biomass δ13C from 3038.60 ‰ to 3503.65‰. Bulk OD600 increased in nanoscale zero-valent iron cultures, although extracellular lactate dehydrogenase release was 37.4% higher than with mZVI, consistent with greater membrane damage. With 10  mM succinate, mZVI increased the coculture peak OD600 from 0.682 to 0.927. Ferrozine lowered the mZVI-associated biomass response by 13-31% but did not abolish it, indicating that soluble Fe(II) contributed without fully accounting for the phenotype. Microscale magnetite produced a comparable peak OD600 (0.813), although its reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) cycling precluded attribution to solid-state conduction alone. A lactate-nitrate diagnostic assay showed that the additional coculture growth was not reproduced by cell-free spent medium or membrane separation, indicating a requirement for close association. Extracellular appendages, enhanced anodic currents, increased expression of S. oneidensis electron-transfer genes and R. palustris carbon-assimilation genes, and lower pioABC expression were consistent with mineral-associated interspecies electron transfer beyond soluble Fe(II) shuttling. However, the relative contributions of direct contact, flavins and surface iron cycling remain unresolved. The response required illumination. Microscale iron minerals may therefore provide a biocompatible electron-transfer interface for CO2-fixing consortia at illuminated anoxic biointerfaces.

item.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Terra
item.abstract: Bringing fast and capable computer use to everyone

cards.score_reason: GPT-6.1新模型发布，重要
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 发布 GPT-6.1 Terra
cards.one_liner: OpenAI 推出 GPT-6.1 Terra，主打面向所有人提供快速且强大的计算机操作能力。
key_findings: 新模型命名为 GPT-6.1 Terra，由 OpenAI 官方发布
核心卖点是快速、能力强的 computer use，面向所有用户
摘要未披露参数、基准测试或定价等具体数据
cards.why_it_matters: 更强的 computer use 意味着可自动操作实验记录、数据库与仪器软件，对合成生物学湿实验流程自动化与数据管理有潜在价值。

item.title: Working with academic communities to build scientific understanding
item.abstract: OpenAI shares model results on the Kakeya conjecture, Exponential Time Hypothesis, and quantum chromodynamics—and how researchers can verify and build on them.

cards.score_reason: 大模型攻克数学难题，科研相关
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 与学术社区合作，推进科学理解
cards.one_liner: OpenAI 公布模型在 Kakeya 猜想、ETH 与量子色动力学上的结果，供研究者验证。
key_findings: 模型在 Kakeya 猜想、指数时间假设、量子色动力学三个数学与物理问题上给出结果。
OpenAI 强调与学术社区合作，公开结果供研究者验证与继续推进。
cards.why_it_matters: AI 辅助数学与理论物理的产出开始进入可验证阶段，合成生物学研究者可关注其方法迁移到通路设计与模型推断的潜力。

item.title: Tesla gave up the EV crown. Now it wants to win the autonomy race.
item.abstract: Tesla hopes autonomy subscriptions can deliver the margins car sales cannot.

cards.score_reason: 特斯拉自动驾驶战略，关注领域
cards.title_cn: 特斯拉放弃电动车王冠，转向自动驾驶竞赛
cards.one_liner: 特斯拉寄望自动驾驶订阅带来汽车销售无法实现的利润率。
key_findings: 特斯拉不再追求电动车销量领先，转向自动驾驶赛道。
公司希望通过自动驾驶订阅服务提升利润率。
汽车销售利润承压，订阅模式被视为新增长点。
cards.why_it_matters: 对合成生物学读者而言，这反映生物医药之外的高科技产业正从硬件销售转向软件订阅变现，可作为技术商业化模式参考。

item.title: Greptile takes bug detection beyond code review with GPT-6 Astra
item.abstract: How Greptile uses GPT-6 Astra to test user workflows, Daybreak to strengthen security, and Codex to reduce rework.

cards.score_reason: GPT-6 Astra应用落地，值得关注

cards.one_liner: Greptile 用 GPT-6 Astra 测试用户工作流，并用 Daybreak 与 Codex 分别强化安全、减少返工。
key_findings: Greptile 将缺陷检测从代码审查扩展到用户工作流测试，由 GPT-6 Astra 驱动。
Daybreak 用于强化安全，Codex 用于减少返工，三者构成组合工具链。
消息来自 OpenAI News，属于 AI 辅助软件工程的产品动态。
cards.why_it_matters: 对合成生物学研发团队而言，这类 AI 工具可把质控从代码层延伸到实验流程与数据管线，降低自动化平台的缺陷与返工成本。

item.abstract: CodeRabbit uses GPT-6.1 Sol to investigate security risks across complex codebases. Its security agent helps developers review findings and proposed fixes.

key_findings: 安全智能体可跨复杂代码库定位安全风险
辅助开发者复核发现的问题与拟议修复方案
由 OpenAI 官方渠道披露的客户应用案例
cards.why_it_matters: 合成生物学团队代码与实验数据管线日益复杂，AI 代码安全审查可降低漏洞与合规风险，值得关注其落地效果。

item.title: How Ultrafast cut incident investigation from hours to minutes at OpenAI
item.abstract: See how OpenAI engineers use Codex Ultrafast to investigate incidents in minutes. Explore faster security analysis, code refactoring, and daily workflows.

cards.score_reason: Codex工程应用，常规参考

cards.one_liner: OpenAI 工程师借助 Codex Ultrafast，把事故调查时间从数小时压缩到数分钟。
